messages:
Ash (PM): heads up — we need a quick tie-break on the acceptance criteria for chat -> rerank fallback. Customer X says rerank must preserve top-3 ordering within 95% of queries, but eng wants looser for latency.
Dan (Eng): can you paste the customer's SLA? 95% top-3 sounds tight for some long-context flows.
Liam (CS): customer emailed: 'we use rerank to boost recall on search widgets; dropping top-3 changes UX badly.' they asked for 95% but said they can accept 90% if latency improves.
Maya (ML): important to clarify: is that 95% relative to the original model baseline or vs current production? big difference.
Ash (PM): good point. Customer means vs their current on-prem model (same model family).
Kevin (Design): from UX side we prefer stable top-3 — users scan first few results. if we go to 90% we should add an annotation 'reranked' to avoid confusion.
Dan (Eng): technical trade: maintaining 95% requires we keep full rerank model w/ cross-encoder which adds ~120ms p50 to path for chat completions. 90% we can hit with a lightweight dual-tower + calibration at ~40ms.
Maya (ML): dual-tower diag: often misses fine-grain swaps in top-3 when queries are short + lots of near-duplicate candidates. for customer examples we should run their corpus through both to get an empirical delta.
Ash (PM): proposal: make acceptance criteria parameterized per-customer tier: - Enterprise SLO: >=95% top-3 (cross-encoder), - Standard: >=90% top-3 (dual-tower). We default to Standard and allow Enterprise via opt-in. Thoughts?
Liam (CS): customer X is enterprise but hasn't signed Dedicated contract yet. they'd likely pay for Enterprise level. worth offering trial?
Nadia (SRE): ops note: cross-encoder path requires GPU for batching; we need to reserve capacity. If we default Enterprise for a big customer it impacts Dedicated pool. we should gate by capacity checks.
Dan (Eng): if we do opt-in Enterprise, dev effort: - routing policy for variant (cross-encoder vs dual-tower) - telemetry to measure top-3 preservation per customer - canary rollout flags. Est time: 2 sprints.
Ash (PM): acceptable. Add canary + automatic fallback if latency exceeds threshold. fallback should revert to dual-tower and surface a metric.
Maya (ML): acceptance test set: we need customer-supplied queries + 5k synthetic near-duplicate examples. pass = measured top-3 preservation >= threshold over testset and p50 latency <= configured SLO.
Kevin (Design): add requirement: show subtle UI hint when rerank variant differs from baseline (e.g., small badge). Keeps users informed.
Liam (CS): I'll ask customer for their query dump and permission to run offline evals. ETA end of week.
Dan (Eng): implementation detail: telemetry event we need: `rerank.variant`, `rerank.latency_ms`, `rerank.topk_preserve` and `customer_id`. simple schema.
Ash (PM): acceptance criteria (draft): - System supports two rerank variants: `cross_encoder` and `dual_tower`. - Default for new customers: `dual_tower`. - Enterprise opt-in toggles `cross_encoder` routing. - For opt-in, offline eval must show >=95% top-3 preservation vs customer's baseline. - Live canary must show p50 latency <= 130ms for cross_encoder and failure autocut at 200ms. - UI badge displayed when cross_encoder used. - Rollout docs + runbook exist.
Maya (ML): small tweak: change 'top-3 preservation' wording to 'top-3 ordering delta <= 5% (per-query strict match)'. clearer metric.
Ash (PM): noted. update criterion accordingly.
Dan (Eng): FYI: for fallback we will implement policy: if 5-minute rolling average latency > threshold OR error rate > 0.5% -> switch to dual_tower. Deployable via feature flag.
Nadia (SRE): add alert: `rerank.variant.switches` and dashboard for variant distribution. also need quota calc for cross-encoder GPU hours.
Liam (CS): customer asked for SLA clause language. draft: 'When customer opts into cross-encoder rerank, Redwood commits to top-3 ordering preservation >=95% subject to job constraints; fallback allowed for operational safety.'
Kevin (Design): quick UI mock requested. I'll drop a link: https://figma.com/s/redwood/rerank-badge (placeholder).
Ash (PM): next steps: Liam to get customer corpus, Dan + Maya to run offline eval, Kevin to produce mock, Nadia to estimate infra impact. we'll reconvene Tues morning for final PRD signoff.
deploy-bot: scheduled message: reminder — weekly PRD sync in #product on Tue 10:00am.
Ash (PM): thanks all :rocket:
__note: This thread captures a short product-spec tie-break discussion; messages intentionally concise to mimic Slack style.
